issues.legal_issue: Open spaces reserved in an approved subdivision layout cannot be used for construction merely because a later, broader development plan shows the area as residential.
material_facts: A layout subdividing a large allotted area was submitted by the allottee’s architect and approved by the municipal authority.
The approved layout identified two sub-plots as open spaces or gardens, while the other plots were used for construction.
A later development plan for the larger scheme showed the area containing the two sub-plots as residential but did not show the internal subdivisions or the open spaces in the approved layout.
The allottee sought to build on the two sub-plots, asserting that the earlier layout was temporary and that open-space requirements were met elsewhere in the larger scheme.
The High Court prohibited construction on the two sub-plots, and the allottee challenged that decision on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were dismissed. The two sub-plots must remain open spaces and cannot be used for construction; the later development plan does not displace their status under the approved layout.
issues.legal_principle: Under Regulation 39 of the Development Control Rules, 1967, layouts or subdivisions of qualifying holdings had to reserve a specified portion for recreational space. Sections 302 and 302-A of the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888, required statutory approval for layouts dividing land into plots. The 1991 Development Control Regulations also required open spaces in relevant layouts or subdivisions. A broad development plan indicating general land use does not override open spaces reserved in an approved internal layout, and the governing scheme did not recognize a temporary layout. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_open_space_protection and approved_subdivision_layout and sites_marked_as_open_space and later_broad_plan_shows_residential_use and other_plots_used_under_layout

predicates.appeal_challenges_open_space_protection: A party appealed a decision protecting open spaces identified in an approved layout.
predicates.approved_subdivision_layout: A competent authority approved a layout subdividing a larger holding into plots.
predicates.sites_marked_as_open_space: The approved layout identified particular plots as open space or garden.
predicates.later_broad_plan_shows_residential_use: A later plan for a larger area showed the relevant area as residential without depicting the internal layout details.
predicates.other_plots_used_under_layout: Other plots in the approved layout were used for construction while the designated open-space plots remained open.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges protection of open spaces in an approved subdivision layout, and a later broad plan shows residential use while other plots have been used under that layout, the designated open spaces remain unavailable for construction.
